source_text: Apostolum ex hoc laudasse libidinem, quia usum feminae dixit esse naturalem, ubi ait, quosdam relicto naturali usu feminae, exarsisse in appetitum suum in invicem
pass_a_gloss: Apostle from this laudasse lust, because usum feminae he-said to-be naturalem, where he-says, quosdam relicto naturali usu feminae, exarsisse in appetitum his-own in mutually.

lemmas.lexica: LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature

pass_b_english: The apostle praised sexual desire by calling the use of a woman natural, when he said that some men “abandoned the natural use of the woman and burned in their desire for one another” (Romans 1:27).

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Paul in Julian's citations; keep Apostle not 'Paul' unless Paulus is written.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

bible_refs.note: Linked from Julian's wording or a clear allusion in the excerpt.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
